overview: Kamo’s settings tune his low-health passive, steerable blood pool, arrow upgrades, and charged blood attacks.
technicalOverview: Noritoshi Kamo's nine unique rows are zero-based slots in CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterUnique. They feed a blood-manipulation kit: a low-HP passive and shared resource helper, a steerable blood pool, an arrow-upgrading normal attack, a counter stance, a cursed-energy blood shot, and a chargeable blood beam. Each row is a plain FloatValue array read by index with no bounds checks. Everything below is traced from reconstructed source: values are CP_190-specific, and same-named rows for other characters are not assumed to behave the same way.

CP_190.title: Character base and blood-resource tuning
CP_190.overview: The character's own row holds the low-HP passive threshold and the two numbers that decide how blood spending becomes either gauge loss or self-damage. It is read both by the HP-change callback and by the controller's shared spend helper.

0.label: Self-damage multiplier
0.simple: Sets how strongly a blood cost damages the owner when the blood gauge is not active.
0.technical: In SpendUnknown2C8, after the supplied Value has been multiplied into Rate, the no-gauge branch requires Rate > 0 and owner GAISlot141 (send-damage rate) > 0. It then calls GetHitPointAfterDamage(row0[0] * Rate), clamps the result to at least 1.0 HP, and writes it back with SetHitPoint. The blood-gauge branch does not read this float; it subtracts Rate from the gauge instead.

1.label: Low-HP passive threshold
1.simple: Turns the CP-190 passive on once HP is at or below this fraction of maximum.
1.technical: OnHitPointChanged computes NewHitPoint / StatusController.HitPointMax and tests row0[1] >= Ratio, so the inclusive boundary is Ratio <= 0.5. On a state change it adds BUFF_CP_190_PASSIVE when low, or removes all CP_190_Passive buff/debuff states when no longer low; unchanged states return early.

2.label: Passive cost rate
2.simple: Makes blood costs cheaper while the CP-190 passive is stacked.
2.technical: In SpendUnknown2C8, GetBuffDebuffStack(CP_190_Passive) > 0 selects row0[2] as Rate instead of the literal 1.0f; the spend Value is then multiplied into Rate. With the default, every later cost is 0.25 * Value while stacked and 1.0 * Value without the stack.

notes.text: The spend helper's self-damage branch is also gated by the owner's send-damage rate; if that rate is not positive, no HP write occurs even when the cost is positive.

CP_190_ATTACKD.title: Blood-pool placement and steering
CP_190_ATTACKD.overview: NormalAttack_2_1 and its air variant use this row to pick where the blood pool is placed, how far it can reach a target, how fast it slides with the stick, and how long/large it becomes. The setup is traced in the controller and action classes.

0.label: Forward placement reach
0.simple: Chooses how far in front of the character the pool appears when there is no selected target.
0.technical: Counter 1 tick sets Target.X/Y = owner XY + owner 2-D facing * row1[0]. If a valid secondary target exists, that point is replaced by cone/cap logic, so this value governs the no-secondary-target placement.

1.label: Steering time limit
1.simple: Caps how long the placed pool can be pushed around.
1.technical: Counter 3 adds DeltaTime to Elapsed every tick. At action start count 1, the action ends when the spot is more than 90 degrees off forward, NormalAttack_2 is no longer held, or row1[1] <= Elapsed. The comparison is inclusive once elapsed reaches 1.5 seconds.

2.label: Target pull cap
2.simple: Prevents a targeted pool placement from being farther away than this distance.
2.technical: With a secondary target inside the aim cone, the 2-D distance is compared with row1[2]. If larger, placement uses owner + normalized delta * row1[2]; if not, it uses the target's location. Outside the cone the closest point on the cone edge is used and this cap is not applied.

3.label: Aim cone width
3.simple: Sets the width of the cone used to decide whether a target can pull the pool directly.
3.technical: AngleBetweenDegrees(owner forward, target direction) > row1[3] * 0.5 selects the outside-cone branch. With the default 90 the half-angle is 45 degrees; outside, the edge direction sign is row1[3] * +0.5 or * -0.5 from the cross-product Z sign before FindClosestPointOnLine.

4.label: Pool steering speed
4.simple: Sets how fast move input slides the pool.
4.technical: Counter 3 computes Goal = PoolLocation + InputMoveDirection * row1[4] * DeltaTime, then resolves ground and wall sweeps. The explicit multiplication by frame delta makes it a distance-per-second rate in world coordinates.

5.label: Pool size
5.simple: Sets the puddle/decal size and the visual scale of pool effects.
5.technical: Passed to AddBloodPool as Radius. It becomes the decal Size.Y and Size.Z, the Niagara 'Radius' parameter, capsule radius/requested capsule size, half of the nine drop-point offsets, FX_CP_190_04311 XY scale as Radius * 0.01, and landed drop effect scale as Radius * 0.002.

6.label: Placement delay
6.simple: Waits before the placed pool begins forming drops.
6.technical: AddBloodPool stores row1[6] as StartDelay. UpdateBloodPools state 0 subtracts DeltaTime divided by owner CustomTimeDilation (or by 1.0 when that value is not positive) and breaks while StartDelay > 0. At <= 0 it re-grounds the centre, probes water, starts the pool sound and advances to state 1.

7.label: Pool formation delay
7.simple: Waits before the pool body and its drops appear.
7.technical: Stored as PoolDelay. State 1 subtracts the same time-dilated delta and breaks while > 0. At <= 0 it spawns FX_CP_190_04111, applies the radius to Niagara/capsules, queues nine surface-dependent drops at 0.2 + index * 0.1 seconds, and advances to state 2.

8.label: Pool lifetime
8.simple: Controls how long the completed pool remains before cleanup.
8.technical: Stored as Lifetime. State 2 subtracts the time-dilated delta; while > 0 queued drops land. At <= 0 all pool effects finish, the decal fades, the sound stops over 0.5 seconds and the pool entry is removed.

notes.text: Pool timers use the owner's CustomTimeDilation divisor; this is a runtime timing detail and not a separate data slot.
Drops use FX_CP_190_04112 for most mapped surfaces and FX_CP_190_04122 for Water; this is effect selection, not another float in the row.

CP_190_ATTACKD_SHOOT_CAMERA.title: Blood-pool aim camera
CP_190_ATTACKD_SHOOT_CAMERA.overview: Camera request row used when NormalAttack_2_1 first enters camera mode 2. MakeUniqueCameraRequest reads indices 0 through 10; the same row's index 6 is also used when leaving the aim camera.

0.label: Camera offset X
0.simple: Moves the aim camera along its local X offset.
0.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2, Row) copies unique float 0 into Request.CameraOffset.X. The virtual camera adds CameraOffset in gaze-rotation space from the eye base.

1.label: Camera offset Y
1.simple: Sets the aim camera's sideways offset.
1.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2, Row) copies unique float 1 into Request.CameraOffset.Y. Zero means no sideways offset; the value is still read and stored.

2.label: Camera offset Z
2.simple: Sets the aim camera's vertical offset.
2.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2, Row) copies unique float 2 into Request.CameraOffset.Z; the virtual camera adds it after rotating by the gaze.

3.label: Down elevation limit
3.simple: Limits how far below the eye the aim camera looks.
3.technical: Copied to Request.LimitAngleDown. The mode-2 camera compares gaze elevation with this limit when the target is below the eye; it is an angle in the rotator/elevation system used by the camera.

4.label: Up elevation limit
4.simple: Limits how far above the eye the aim camera looks.
4.technical: Copied to Request.LimitAngleUp. The mode-2 camera compares gaze elevation with this limit when the target is above the eye; it is an angle in the camera's rotator/elevation system.

5.label: Field of view
5.simple: Sets the aim camera's FOV only when positive.
5.technical: Copied to Request.FieldOfView. ChangeCameraMode applies a new FOV only when it is > 0; zero therefore leaves the FOV unchanged on entry, rather than setting FOV to zero.

6.label: FOV blend time
6.technical: Copied to Request.FieldOfViewBlendTime. On camera exit CP_190 explicitly sets FOV 90 and reuses this same row index as the blend time; a positive value starts FovInterp, otherwise the FOV snaps.

7.label: FOV easing selector
7.technical: Read as an integer switch: 0 = Linear, 1 = EaseIn, 2 = EaseOut, 3 = EaseInOut; other values leave the request's default easing. The entry FOV here is zero, so this mainly matters when a positive exit FOV is blended.

8.label: Orbit yaw
8.technical: Copied to Request.OrbitYaw and applied by the mode-2 camera as gaze orbit about the camera (rotator yaw).

9.label: Orbit pitch
9.technical: Copied to Request.OrbitPitch and applied as rotator pitch in the mode-2 camera request.

10.label: Camera roll
10.technical: Copied to Request.Roll; the virtual camera consumes Roll in its request update.

notes.text: The camera is restored only when the next action is AttackDefault and the camera is still in mode 2; the exit request forces FOV 90 and takes its blend time from this row's index 6.

CP_190_ATTACKE.title: Arrow-upgrade normal attack
CP_190_ATTACKE.overview: NormalAttack_3 and its air variant use this row to time the one-shot weapon upgrade and pay for it through the CP-190 resource helper. The upgraded attack row is a different table, not a second unique float row.

0.label: Upgrade delay
0.simple: Sets how long the normal attack waits before upgrading the arrows.
0.technical: In start count 1, ActionElapsedTime accumulates DeltaTime. When UpgradeCount == 0 and !(row3[0] >= ActionElapsedTime) — that is, after elapsed time is strictly greater than 0.1 — the action increments UpgradeCount, resets elapsed to zero, plays FX_CP_190_00101 at L_weapon, calls UpgradeSpawnedEffects and spends row3[1]. At exactly 0.1 no upgrade occurs.

1.label: Upgrade blood cost
1.simple: Sets the blood cost paid once when the arrows upgrade.
1.technical: Passed as the Value argument to UCP_190_ActionController::SpendUnknown2C8 at the same one-shot upgrade. Its effective gauge or HP cost is scaled by the passive-rate and self-damage rules in row 0.

notes.text: After the upgrade, attack index 2 resolves to CP_190_ATTACKE_02_01 instead of the normal set row; that row lookup is separate from this unique row.

CP_190_ATTACKF.title: Counter stance
CP_190_ATTACKF.overview: NormalAttack_3_1 and its air variant use this row for the counter shot's blood cost, the stance's open window, and the hit-slow applied to an attacker who hits the open stance.

0.label: Counter-shot blood cost
0.simple: Sets the resource paid when the counter shot fires.
0.technical: On UniqueAction parameter 0, the action plays FX_CP_190_00401_1 or _00501_1 from PG_Attack_01 with the boot rotation and passes row4[0] to SpendUnknown2C8.

1.label: Stance open duration
1.simple: Sets how long the character holds the counter stance.
1.technical: Phase 1 adds DeltaTime to ActionElapsedTime and returns while row4[1] > ActionElapsedTime. At elapsed >= 0.6 it plays the end animation and clears bStanceOpen, so the boundary is inclusive when the timer reaches the value.

2.label: Counter hit-slow rate
2.simple: Sets the hit-slow rate applied to the attacker on a counter.
2.technical: BuildHitResponse sets AttackerHitSlowRate = row4[2] whenever the open stance takes the hit and sets bAttackerHitSlow true.

3.label: Counter hit-slow time
3.simple: Sets how long the attacker is hit-slowed.
3.technical: BuildHitResponse sets AttackerHitSlowTime = row4[3] in the same response. It also sets the instigator as secondary target and locks collision key 9.

notes.text: Hits whose damage row has bIgnoreHyperArmor are not intercepted by the stance, regardless of these values.

CP_190_ATTACKG.title: Cursed-energy shot cost
CP_190_ATTACKG.overview: CursedEnergyAttack_1 chooses one of the first three floats by cursed-energy level and pays that amount through the CP-190 resource helper when the blood shot starts.

0.label: Level 1 blood cost
0.simple: Blood cost of the level 1 cursed-energy shot.
0.technical: On UniqueAction parameter 0 at start count 0, GetCursedEnergyLevel() 1 selects LevelIndex 0. The shot variant is FX_CP_190_00401 when the gauge/pool is live, else FX_CP_190_00501. row5[0] is passed to SpendUnknown2C8.

1.label: Level 2 blood cost
1.simple: Blood cost of the level 2 cursed-energy shot.
1.technical: GetCursedEnergyLevel() 2 selects LevelIndex 1; row5[1] is passed to SpendUnknown2C8 at the same one-shot start.

2.label: Level 3 blood cost
2.simple: Blood cost of the level 3 cursed-energy shot.
2.technical: GetCursedEnergyLevel() 3 selects LevelIndex 2; row5[2] is passed to SpendUnknown2C8 at the same one-shot start.

notes.text: Any level outside 1 through 3 leaves LevelIndex at its default 0 in the traced switch, so it uses the level 1 float rather than an out-of-bounds row read.

CP_190_ATTACKH.title: Blood-beam charge and growth
CP_190_ATTACKH.overview: This row drives the charged beam: opening cost, four charge-stage thresholds and maximum lengths, four growth speeds, and one fixed growth speed used by the auto variants. The beam is clipped by traces after growth.

0.label: Beam opening blood cost
0.simple: Resource paid when the blood beam shot starts.
0.technical: On UniqueAction parameter 0, CP_190 plays FX_CP_190_00401 or _00501 from PG_Attack_01, attaches it KeepWorld, and passes row7[0] to SpendUnknown2C8.

1.label: Stage 0 max beam length
1.simple: Maximum beam length for charge stage 0.
1.technical: UpdateMaxBeamLength stores row7[1] in MaxBeamLength at ChargeStage 0; TickBeam caps BeamLength with FMath::Min(Grown, MaxBeamLength). The visible direct caller is the early-release branch when ShouldKeepCharging is false.

2.label: Stage 0 charge time
2.technical: In start count 1 ChargeStage 0 advances when row7[2] < ActionElapsedTime, resets elapsed and calls StepChargeStage. The strict `<` means no advance at exact equality; 4500 is seconds of accumulated action time.

3.label: Stage 1 max beam length
3.simple: Maximum beam length for charge stage 1.
3.technical: UpdateMaxBeamLength assigns row7[3] when ChargeStage == 1; the same cap is applied in TickBeam.

4.label: Stage 1 charge time
4.simple: Time needed before stage 1 advances, with a level gate.
4.technical: ChargeStage 1 advances only when row7[4] < ActionElapsedTime and GetCursedEnergyLevel() > 1. Equality does not advance; the level gate is strictly greater than level 1.

5.label: Stage 2 max beam length
5.simple: Maximum beam length for charge stage 2.
5.technical: UpdateMaxBeamLength assigns row7[5] when ChargeStage == 2. The auto beam variant overrides the whole function and always uses row7[5] as its maximum.

6.label: Stage 2 charge time
6.simple: Time needed before stage 2 advances, with a level gate.
6.technical: ChargeStage 2 advances only when row7[6] < ActionElapsedTime and GetCursedEnergyLevel() > 2. Equality does not advance; the level gate is strictly greater than level 2.

7.label: Stage 3 max beam length
7.simple: Maximum beam length for the last charge stage.
7.technical: UpdateMaxBeamLength assigns row7[7] when ChargeStage == 3. The main tick has no further stage advancement beyond 3.

8.label: Stage 0 beam growth speed
8.simple: How fast the beam grows at charge stage 0.
8.technical: GetBeamGrowSpeed returns row7[8] for ChargeStage 0. TickBeam computes Grown = speed * DeltaTime + BeamLength and then caps it at MaxBeamLength.

9.label: Stage 1 beam growth speed
9.simple: How fast the beam grows at charge stage 1.
9.technical: GetBeamGrowSpeed returns row7[9] for ChargeStage 1, with the same per-frame growth and cap.

10.label: Stage 2 beam growth speed
10.simple: How fast the beam grows at charge stage 2.
10.technical: GetBeamGrowSpeed returns row7[10] for ChargeStage 2, with the same per-frame growth and cap.

11.label: Stage 3 beam growth speed
11.simple: How fast the beam grows at the final charge stage.
11.technical: GetBeamGrowSpeed returns row7[11] for ChargeStage 3. Any other stage falls back to the literal 30000.0f rather than to this row.

12.label: Auto beam growth speed
12.simple: Fixed growth speed used by the auto beam variants.
12.technical: TCP_190_CursedEnergyAttack_2_Auto overrides GetBeamGrowSpeed and always returns row7[12], ignoring ChargeStage. The ordinary 74/78 variants keep using the per-stage speeds in indices 8 through 11.

notes.text: Beam length growth is separate from visual effect choice: GetBeamEffectId indexes GCP_190_BeamEffectIds by cursed-energy level and stage, not by these float values.
The ordinary variants keep charging while within 0.05 s of the notify start or while CursedEnergyAttack_2 is held; the auto variants only keep charging within the first 0.05 s.

11.label: Shared trap-only row 8 slot 11
11.simple: Zero in CP_190's beam camera row; no CP_190-specific effect is traced here.
11.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest reads only unique indices 0 through 10, so this CP_190 action never consumes it. Uzumaki trap uses it as a minimum-distance clamp for the source actor. That is a different actor/controller path and is not assigned to CP_190; no CP_190-specific effect is established.

notes.text: Indices 11 through 13 are not read by MakeUniqueCameraRequest, which stops at index 10. A generic Uzumaki trap reads source-interface row8 floats 11/12/13, but no CP_190 action path here reaches that trap reader.

Row indices are positional: CharacterDataTable lists Id_CharacterUnique in order, AGameCharacter loads one optional unique row per name, and the accessor reads UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] with no bounds checks.

The two GUF helpers are thin forwarders: FGameCharacterAction::GetOwnerUniqueFloat calls AGameCharacter::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue, and MakeUniqueCameraRequest is the shared reader for camera rows, filling only indices 0 through 10 when CameraMode is 2.

All blood costs run through UCP_190_ActionController::SpendUnknown2C8. With CP_190_Passive stacked the rate starts at row 0 index 2 (0.25), otherwise at literal 1.0; if the blood gauge is live the scaled value is subtracted from it, while otherwise a positive send-damage rate allows HP to be reduced with a floor of 1.
Ground and air action variants share these same unique rows and generally reuse the ground attack-set row on slot 141; there are no separate air-specific unique rows in CP_190's nine-row list.

The blood pools live on the controller, are stepped last-to-first with owner CustomTimeDilation, and water ground changes the drop effect to FX_CP_190_04122 while other mapped surfaces use FX_CP_190_04112.

Auto CursedEnergyAttack_2 variants (types 75/79) are not just shorter holds: they disable target aim, keep charging only within the first 0.05 s, use a fixed beam effect, take growth speed from row 7 index 12, and take max length from row 7 index 5.

No character-specific .inl is included by CP_190; its controller includes ordinary headers, and the shared GameCharacterActionInline.h fast GUF path is used by CP_270 rather than by CP_190, so the CP_190 reads are the traced out-of-line calls shown above.

The CP_190 verification record is byte-compare work on reconstructed actions; it documents several matched slot bodies but also recorded drift and parked/decoded bodies, so these wiki explanations should be read as source-traced behavior rather than a claim that every retail function is byte-identical.

Weapon visuals are a separate quirk: UniqueAction 100/101/102 attach FX_CP_190_00211 to arrow_A1/B1/C1 and 200 attaches FX_CP_190_09101 to arrow_A1; arrow material sections are hidden at setup and hidden/shown with battle sequences. These calls do not read the unique float rows.

The generic trap controller reads source-interface row 7 and row 8 floats for its own Uzumaki behavior. Those reads are not CP_190 readers: CP_190's traced row 7/8 consumers are the blood-beam actions and MakeUniqueCameraRequest, so the trap-only tail of row 8 is marked unresolved rather than assigned.
